LogEx controlled gRPC output ownership (Tonic 0.13.1)

The complete published crate is retained, including its license, original README,
lockfile and 67-file upstream inventory. No Tonic version upgrade.
Archive SHA-256: 7e581ba15a835f4d9ea06c55ab1bd4dce26fc53752c69a04aac00703bfb49ba9
Published VCS commit: b303caa52ba8bbe8172310be7165a80b7c2a53f8
Inventory: LOGEX-UPSTREAM-SHA256
Exact local modifications/additions: LOGEX-PATCH.diff

Encoder::uses_prepared_buffers and prepare opt into exact payload preparation.
PreparedEncode carries an exact unframed length and one allocator identity.
EncodeBufferAllocator admits requested capacity before returning an empty,
uniquely owned OwnedEncodeBuffer. The caller reconciles actual capacity and
retains its guard; backing drops before the opaque guard. Prepared mode starts
without an output allocation. It checks lengths and configured send limits,
admits replacement capacity while the old buffer is alive, and restricts every
EncodeBuf mutation to the prepared span. Incorrect trusted encoder lengths are
internal errors (infallible BufMut overflow retains its usual panic contract).
Preparation/allocation statuses, including RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, are preserved.

Prepared flushes transfer the complete buffer to Bytes::from_owner; no shared
spare tail is reused. Final clones/slices retain the full backing charge. Batch
readiness and yield thresholds are preserved. A changed allocator identity is
rejected before writing. Prepared compression is explicitly unsupported; default
unconfigured compression remains available. The bytes minimum is now 1.9, which
introduced from_owner; the workspace remains locked to bytes 1.11.1. The upstream
standalone lock remains unchanged at bytes 1.10.1. Its tests and the workspace
integration controls validate both pinned contexts. Reference-count/control
metadata remains outside allocation-capacity accounting; this is not an RSS cap.

Lifecycle fixes also apply to default encoders: initialize the five-byte header
before fallible encoding; discard incomplete output on encoder error; latch
terminal stream/body state for client and server, and drop the pinned source.
A source error still flushes already-valid buffered data before its non-success
status. The default BufMut test now initializes its bytes before advancing.
Safety comments cover the delegated unsafe BufMut contract. The sole unrelated
source cleanup scopes the server pin macro import to its existing TLS feature,
so default-feature builds do not gain an unused-import warning from vendoring.

The LogEx codec continues to invoke Prost and uses generated service routing.
It checks query health/cancellation before preparation, allocation and encoding,
and after a single admitted synchronous Prost message before publication. That
message is the cooperative cancellation boundary, not a hard CPU-latency limit.
No protobuf schema or generated client type change. Metadata-only RPCs keep the
ordinary codec. Controlled response compression is not enabled by LogEx.

Run default and gzip library controls with the repository's pinned compiler:
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/tonic-regressions cargo test --manifest-path vendor/tonic/Cargo.toml --lib --locked
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/tonic-regressions cargo test --manifest-path vendor/tonic/Cargo.toml --lib --features gzip --locked
Tests use the pinned compiler's Waker::noop; production additions retain the
upstream stated MSRV syntax. Existing upstream loopback fixtures require local
bind permission. All added ownership/lifecycle controls are tiny offline cases.
